title: A sign-up form that works without a mouse

terminal.description: The page runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. The shell is here if you want to look around the files.

tasks.title: Tie every label to its field
tasks.description:
Give every field of the sign-up form a label that belongs to it.

The check finds the fields by their `name` attributes, so keep those: `name`, `email`, `phone`, `people`, `newsletter` and the two radio buttons named `event`.

For each field it checks that a `<label>` is tied to it, either by wrapping the field or by a `for` attribute that matches the field's `id`, and that the label has text. Each radio button needs its own label.
nextSteps: Click the words "Your name" in the Browser panel and notice nothing happens.
Give the name field an `id` and wrap its text in a `label` that points at it.
Do the same for email, phone and how many people.
Wrap each radio button and the checkbox together with its words in a `label`, then press Check.
hints: Text that sits next to a field is just text. A screen reader landing on the field hears nothing.
There are two ways to tie a label to a field: put the field inside the label, or give the label a `for` that matches the field's `id`.
For the radio buttons and the checkbox, wrapping is the shortest: one `label` around the input and the words after it.

tasks.title: Ask for the right kind of answer
tasks.description:
Tell the browser what each field expects, so it can bring up the right keyboard and stop a form that is not ready.

The check looks for:

- `name` is required
- `email` has the email type and is required
- `phone` has the phone number type and is not required
- `people` is a number field with a smallest value of `1` and a largest of `6`
- one of the `event` radio buttons is required, so a choice must be made
nextSteps: Look at the `type` of each field. They are all `text` right now.
Change the types of email, phone and people.
Add the limits to the people field.
Mark the fields that must be filled in, then press Check.
hints: An input's `type` changes what the browser accepts and, on a phone, which keyboard opens.
One attribute with no value makes a field required. A number field takes two more for its limits.
The types you need are `email`, `tel` and `number`. A radio group is required when any one of its buttons has the attribute.

tasks.title: Group the choices and send with a real button
tasks.description:
Make the form a real form that a keyboard can send.

The check looks for:

- one `<form>` element, and all the fields are inside it
- the two `event` radio buttons are in one `<fieldset>` whose `<legend>` has text
- a submit button inside the form: a `<button>` (with no type, or `type="submit"`) or an `<input type="submit">`, with text on it
- no element with the class `button` that is not a real button

Keep the class `signup` on the form so it keeps its look.
nextSteps: Press Tab in the Browser panel until you reach the yellow button. You never will.
Turn the `div` with class `signup` into a form.
Put the radio buttons in a fieldset and move the question into its legend.
Replace the yellow `div` with a real button, then press Tab again and press Check.
hints: A styled `div` cannot be reached with Tab or pressed with Enter. The right element gets both for free.
A fieldset draws a border and a legend sits in it. A rule in `styles.css` can take the border away if you do not want it.
The question "Which event?" becomes the legend, and the styled `div` at the bottom becomes a button whose type is submit.
